To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the institutional reform in the PAM has been effective in terms of reducing corruption, but it has not yet been effective in terms de l'Etats de droit.

the Arab countries of the Mediterranean have been able to improve their institutions, but that these reforms have not been sufficient to change the institutional architecture of their economies, and that these countries have not been able to develop a system that can constrain the elites and make them implement reforms that will allow the development of a more efficient system of governance.

(1) the reforms of good governance in the Mediterranean Arab countries have been successful in terms of the institutional variables that are measured by MINEFI, (2) the transition of the institutional systems is not complete, (3) the institutional systems are not conducive to the constraints of elites to undertake the reforms necessary for institutional change, (4) the persistence of the inherited institutions and the perpetuation of the clan thinking have rather favoured the predatory organizations and institutions geared toward the rent-seeking.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of institutions in the economic development of the countries of the Mediterranean basin.
understanding the nature of the institutional transformation in the Arab Mediterranean Countries and its implications for economic development.
the role of institutions in the development process of Arab Mediterranean countries (AMCs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Arab countries of the Mediterranean are still far away from the ideal model of good governance and from the rule of law.

the Arab countries are in the process of transition from a system where the state is instrumentalized for private interests through relational and informal arrangements, to a system of institutions based on more transparent mechanisms and more respect for the impersonal rule of law.
the institutional change in the MENA countries is still far from being completed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have tried to understand the evolution of institutions of governance in Mediterranean Arab Countries (MAC) and to assess the role that they play in economic development.
the Arab Mediterranean countries have to go beyond good governance reforms in order to build the rule of law.

the institutional reforms implemented in the PAMs are effective but the systems of governance of the state and the firms, supposed to constrain the discretionary power of the elites, remain weakly binding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reform of institutions of governance in the PAM is not a necessary condition for the emergence of an efficient institutional environment conducive to economic development.

the institutional reforms implemented by the PAM are effective but that the governance systems of the states and enterprises, designed to constrain the discretionary power of the ruling elite, remain weakly constraining.
the transition to good governance in the PAM has not been successful because the institutions of governance have remained weak and the elites continue to resist reforms.
